note: THE NUMBER PURCHASE FORM STOPS ASKING A CHURCH TO GUESS. The founder typed DE into a free-text country box and 615 — a Nashville area code — into a free-text area box, and was told only AFTER pressing a button that 'local numbers in DE can't send or receive SMS. Pick another type', advice about a field the form did not have. THE-330 OWNS the four files below and this is the state it leaves them in. It changes NO send path, NO meter, NO STOP handling and NONE of THE-318's four purchase fixes; sms-optout.ts, firestore.rules, firestore.indexes.json, functions/ and layout.tsx are byte-identical and pinned as such in this ticket's own guard suite.

entries.why: THE FORM BECOMES A SET OF PICKERS DRAWN FROM THE PROVIDER'S LIVE CATALOGUE. Country, number type and area code are all chosen, never typed: every offerable country is listed as 'Germany (DE)' — never a bare code, and the name comes from Intl.DisplayNames because the provider sends only the code — with the ones that cannot text visibly marked and rendering NO Buy button. Every field the provider reports is on screen before the money: per country (name, code, smsAvailable, inStock, monthlyCents, needsKyc, and tier TRANSLATED rather than printed raw), per type in a ui/table matrix (numberType, smsAvailable, whatsappAvailable, callsAvailable, monthlyCents, needsKyc, fulfilment, inStock), and per number as its own features list. Capability is decided by the PER-TYPE flag, never the country-level one that mirrors only the default type — GB mobile texts while GB local does not, and that is the subtle failure this exists to prevent. A failed catalogue fetch renders a FAILURE alert and no picker at all, never an empty list. Primitives: badge, table, item, skeleton and empty adopted; ui/select REJECTED at all three pickers, with both measured reasons named at the call site (it is a listbox button, not a <select>, which would blind the existing width guard; and it pins 32px through an attribute selector that outranks Rule 4). THE-318's purchase path, the KYC 202 handling, the carrier-registration warning above the Buy button and the single justified inline style are untouched.

NEW, AND DELIBERATELY PURE. It holds the provider's response SHAPES and the predicates that decide what a church may buy — smsCapableTypes, countryCanSms, typeIsInstantlyBuyable, purchasableSmsTypes — plus the country name, type label, tier translation and price formatting. It makes no network call, reads no environment, holds no credential and imports NOTHING from zernio.ts; the arrow points the other way, so THE-314's 'there is exactly ONE module that talks to the provider' guard keeps the list it had and the admin screen reads these shapes without pulling the transport into a client bundle. It hardcodes no country, price, tier or capability: every value is read off the fetched catalogue. Prices are the PROVIDER's and are deliberately not routed through formatPlanPrice, and a missing price renders as an em dash rather than as free.

TWO ENDPOINTS THE PROVIDER ALREADY ANSWERED AND NOTHING USED. zernioListCountries reads GET /v1/phone-numbers/countries — which the provider's own documentation describes as driving the country picker — and zernioAreaOptions reads the areaOptions of GET /v1/phone-numbers/availability, so an area code is chosen from live stock instead of guessed against a hard 409. zernioSearchNumbers gains `type` and `contains`, so the preview draws from the pool the purchase will draw from rather than from the country's WhatsApp-safe default. A malformed catalogue answers as a FAILURE, never as zero countries. THE-318's purchase body is untouched, field for field: wantsSms true and not a parameter, connectWhatsapp explicitly false, wantsWhatsapp false, the RETURNED profileId read back, allowMultiple forwarded, and the three purchase response shapes still read distinctly. The webhook signature verifier is unchanged.

TWO NEW READ BRANCHES AND ONE NEW GATE. ?countries=1 serves the catalogue behind the SAME Ministry entitlement as the purchase, memoised in-process for ten minutes and NEVER served past that TTL — a failed refresh answers 502 rather than handing a church a stale rate card it is about to commit to, and fetchedAt rides on the response so the screen can say when it was read. ?areas=1 serves the area options. ?available=1 now carries the chosen type through. The POST accepts a numberType and GATES it server-side against the SMS pool zernioSmsNumberType already resolves, answering 409 TYPE_NOT_SMS_CAPABLE before any money moves — so a client naming a mute type cannot spend a church's money even though the picker would not have offered it. THE-318's own resolution is still what is SENT, an unverifiable lookup still does not block the purchase, and no entitlement is written anywhere.
